_meta.description: Best-effort snapshot of SWIG pcbnew symbols and their kicad-python (kipy) equivalents. Statuses are valid for the kicad_python_version above and may change as the IPC API grows.

pcbnew.note: `import pcbnew` becomes `from kipy import KiCad`; every call goes through a KiCad client object instead of module-level functions.

GetBoard.note: Connect with KiCad() first: board = KiCad().get_board(). The IPC API talks to a running KiCad, so there is no board outside an open document.

LoadBoard.note: The IPC API has no standalone file loader; it operates on documents open in KiCad. Open the board in the PCB editor, or use kicad-cli for batch work.

NewBoard.note: Creating a board file from scratch is not part of the IPC API in this version.

SaveBoard.note: Board.save() writes the open document; Board.save_as(filename, overwrite=...) writes a copy. Only the board currently open in KiCad can be saved.

Refresh.note: There is no explicit redraw call. Wrap edits in Board.begin_commit()/push_commit(); the editor refreshes and the change becomes undoable.

UpdateUserInterface.note: Same as Refresh: the editor updates when a commit is pushed, there is no direct UI hook.

ActionPlugin.note: The IPC plugin system has no base class. Ship a plugin.json declaring your actions plus an entrypoint script that connects with kipy.KiCad(); `swig2ipc skeleton` writes the manifest.

FromMM.note: Returns integer nanometres, the internal unit used throughout kipy.

ToMM.note: Takes integer nanometres and returns millimetres as a float.

IU_PER_MM.note: No scale constant is exported; convert through from_mm()/to_mm() instead of multiplying by a factor.

VECTOR2I.note: Vector2.from_xy(x, y) builds one from integer nanometre coordinates.

wxPoint.note: wxPoint was already removed from the SWIG API in KiCad 7; Vector2 is the IPC equivalent and has no wx dependency.

BOX2I.note: Bounding boxes are returned as Box2 (see Board.get_item_bounding_box).

BOARD.note: A client-side handle on the board document open in KiCad, not an in-memory board file.

FOOTPRINT.note: FootprintInstance is a footprint placed on the board; its library definition is FootprintInstance.definition (kipy.board_types.Footprint).

PCB_ARC.note: Arc-shaped track; Board.get_tracks() returns Track and ArcTrack objects.

PCB_VIA.note: Via geometry lives in its pad stack (Via.padstack).

PAD.note: Pad shape and drill are described by Pad.padstack (kipy.board_types.PadStack).

ZONE.note: Filled areas are available as Zone.filled_polygons.

PCB_TEXTBOX.note: Returned together with BoardText from Board.get_text().

PCB_SHAPE.note: Concrete subclasses are BoardSegment/BoardArc/BoardCircle/BoardRectangle/BoardPolygon/BoardBezier; to_concrete_board_shape() narrows a generic shape.

PCB_GROUP.note: Group.items lists the KIIDs of its members.

PCB_DIMENSION_BASE.note: Concrete kinds are AlignedDimension, OrthogonalDimension, RadialDimension, LeaderDimension and CenterDimension.

NETINFO_ITEM.note: Net has .name and .code; Board.get_nets() lists them.

GetFootprints.note: Returns a sequence of FootprintInstance for the open board.

GetTracks.note: Returns Track and ArcTrack objects. Unlike the SWIG BOARD.GetTracks(), vias are not included: use Board.get_vias().

GetPads.note: Board-wide pad list; pads of one footprint are FootprintInstance.definition.pads.

GetZones.note: Returns Zone objects, including rule areas.

GetDrawings.note: The SWIG drawings list is split up: get_shapes(), get_text(), get_dimensions() and get_reference_images().

GetNetsByName.note: No name-keyed map is returned; get_nets() gives a sequence of Net that you index by .name yourself.

Add.note: BOARD.Add(item) becomes board.create_items(item); the server assigns the new KIIDs.

Remove.note: Also remove_items_by_id() when you only hold KIIDs.

GetPosition.note: Positions are per-type properties rather than one BOARD_ITEM method: FootprintInstance.position, Track.start/.end, BoardText.position, and so on.

SetPosition.note: Assign to the property and push the item back with Board.update_items(); local changes are not sent automatically.

GetLayer.note: Each item type exposes its own .layer property holding a BoardLayer enum value; Board.get_layer_name() turns it into a string.

GetReference.note: The reference is a Field object: footprint.reference_field.text.value.

GetValue.note: The value is a Field object: footprint.value_field.text.value.

GetLayerName.note: Takes a BoardLayer enum value; Board.get_layer_by_name() is the inverse.

GetCopperLayerCount.note: Board.get_enabled_layers() and get_visible_layers() cover the related SWIG calls.

GetTitleBlock.note: Returns a TitleBlockInfo; write it back with set_title_block_info().

GetDesignSettings.note: kipy.board_rules wraps design rule types, but in kicad-python 0.8.0 that module fails to import (its generated protobuf stubs are out of sync) and no Board accessor exists. Stackup and copper layer count are reachable via Board.get_stackup()/get_copper_layer_count().

ZONE_FILLER.note: One call replaces constructing a filler and calling Fill(); it can block until KiCad finishes.

PLOT_CONTROLLER.note: kipy.board_jobs wraps plot/export job settings for the KiCad 11 API, but in kicad-python 0.8.0 that module fails to import (its generated protobuf stubs are out of sync) and no job runner is exposed; call kicad-cli from your plugin to plot.

GetBuildVersion.note: Returns a KiCadVersion; get_api_version() reports the API version of the running instance.

SETTINGS_MANAGER.note: KiCad's settings manager is not exposed over IPC. KiCad.get_plugin_settings_path() gives your plugin a directory for its own settings.
